name: Sangir
confidence_why: one confirmed first-hand source; 7 other works read were silent
catalog_quote: Stress is very largely predictable in San, falling on the penultimate syllable except when the final syllable is əʔ, in which case it falls on the third-last syllable, e.g. líkudəʔ back

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every deciding passage (Sneddon 1984:20, 25, 53) is present verbatim at the stated printed pages in the PDF we hold, and the Adriani 1893:15-16 Dutch corroboration is present in the held scanned. (2) The classification 'fixed-strict, penult, paragogic əʔ invisible' (rule 10/010/0010..) is exactly what Sneddon states twice (synchronic sec. 2.1.1.2 and diachronic sec. 2.3.23) and what Adriani 1893 states independently ('accent in general on the penultimate.. the support vowel carries no weight for stress'). Two independent primary descriptions by the two principal describers of the language, 1893 and 1984, agree. (3) The only unheld primary phonology is Maryott 1961 (16 pp, print-only); nothing newer or instrumental exists per Glottolog (30 refs inspected) and a Crossref query. (4) Minor caveats, not grounds for reclassification: Sneddon hedges 'very largely predictable' and Adriani allows fi

sources.quote: Main quote is English. Adriani 1893:15-16 (Dutch): "The stress falls on the penultimate or on the final syllable. ... The vowel which serves to preserve the original final consonant of a word does form a new syllable with that final consonant, but for the stress it carries no weight. ... 2. The accent falls in general on the penultimate syllable, both in root words and in derived words."
